set.notes: Advanced 2026-09-18. All 17 post-consent modification records for NSW data centre SSDs are harvested and loaded: case ids, stages, decisions, determination dates and LGAs. Fifteen approved, one withdrawn, two undetermined. Five are material to the environmental envelope (added generators and diesel at Roberts Road, a power consumption increase at Eastern Creek, added fuel storage at Lane Cove West, an expansion at Talavera Road, and pending operational-infrastructure changes at Roberts Road again). RESIDUAL: modification pages do not publish the development description, so the QUANTUM of each change is unknown - the underlying modification reports must be fetched (RG-045). Local council development applications are also still out of scope. UPDATED 2026-11-18 (research batch 7): The quantum RG-034 left open is answered by RG-045 from the five modification reports, read today: Eastern Creek 32 MW to 63 MW, Roberts Road 48 to 72 generators (96 proposed), Lane Cove West 116 smaller generators and 1,952 kL of internal fuel storage, Talavera Road 38 MW to 47 MW. Local council development applications remain out of scope. UPDATED 2026-11-18 (research batch 8, second pass): MODIFICATION HALF DONE: all 17 modification records on the NSW data centre files are read (five in batch 7; ten assessment reports and one modification report today; the withdrawn 51 Huntingwood Mod 1 report answered 401). Beyond batch 7's five, three more add generators or diesel. LANE COVE WEST MOD 4 (October 2025, section 4.55(1A), decided by an A/Team Leader, posted on 9 July 2025, not exhibited): 'The proposed modification seeks to increase diesel storage capacity from 1,651 t to 1966.9 t, below the storage limit of 2,000 t specified in condition A6(c)', and lithium-ion batteries from 55 t to 308 t; the Department added conditions 'requiring detailed monitoring and reporting of generator use'. LANCELEY PLACE MOD 2 (April 2026, section 4.55(1A), posted 27 January 2026): from '30 x 2.8 MW / 3.5 MVA generators' to '42 x 2.82 MW / 3.6 MVA generators', 'with associated increases in diesel storage' above the approved 895,000 L. LANE COVE WEST MOD 3 (June 2024, section 4.55(2), exhibited 21 February to 6 March 2023): from '116 transformers / generators' to '121'. The rest change no generator or diesel quantity: Lane Cove West Mod 2 (office use; section 4.55(2), exhibited, seven submissions), 51 Huntingwood Mod 2 ('316 back-up diesel generators (No change)'; lodged by a builder, AW Edwards Pty Ltd), Dexus Estate Mod 7 (layout; restates 1,288,600 L of diesel; not exhibited), Kemps Creek Mod 1 (fit-out before operation), Roberts Road Mod 1 (height), Davis Road Mod 1 (trees), Lanceley Place Mod 3 (switch room), 200 Aldington Mod 8 (an intersection). PROPOSED to the author: reclassify SSD-9741-Mod-4 (change_type other -> fuel_storage_increase, materiality 3 -> 5), SSD-66777221-Mod-2 (other -> generator_increase, 2 -> 5) and SSD-9741-Mod-3 (design -> generator_increase, 2 -> 4). set.notes: ADVANCED 2026-10-22 (research batch 3). Traced to source: Data Centres Australia told the inquiry operators 'will pay $10.3 billion in energy infrastructure to 2030, and $1.1 billion of that is excess capacity'. The report behind the industry's figures (Mandala, commissioned for Data Centres Australia by AirTrunk, AWS, CDC and NEXTDC) gives $3.1bn invested 2020-2025 and $7.2bn forecast to 2030, built from 'data from select data centre operators'; the two make $10.3bn, and the only '$10.3 billion' the report states is the Australian Government's grid funding. Its $1.1bn excess is within the forecast, with $0.5bn before. The networks told the inquiry the principle holds - Ausgrid: 'the customer who caused network costs pays for them'; Transgrid invests only on 'full commitment' and had no data centre commitment on 22 May 2026 - but none put a total on it. Still to test: the quantum against Transgrid, Ausgrid and Endeavour capital plans and AER determinations (aer.gov.au did not answer). UPDATED 2026-11-18 (research batch 8, second pass): Transgrid's own page states the principle and the constraint, not a total: 'Households and businesses should not bear the cost or risk associated with this growth'; capacity in the Sydney basin is 'largely exhausted'; since late 2024 it has received 'data centre connection enquiries totaling more than 10 GW within a 12 km radius of Sydney West'; capacity is allocated only on a signed connection agreement, for loads of 30 MW or more. It puts no dollar figure on what data centres pay. The AER's register closed the connection again today (recorded). The quantum test against the networks' capital plans stays open.

add_sources.quote: Households and businesses should not bear the cost or risk associated with this growth. | Capacity to connect to the transmission network in the Sydney basin is largely exhausted | data centre connection enquiries totaling more than 10 GW within a 12 km radius of Sydney West | network capacity is only allocated upon signature of a Network Connection Agreement (NCA) | an inverter-based load greater than or equal to 30 MW or 30 MVA

set.notes: ADVANCED 2026-10-14. Archived and read the article itself (version of 2026-10-02; it was not archived when first read on 2026-09-18, so that version cannot be shown): it does not mention Vantage, AustralianSuper, AirTrunk SYD3 or Stockland, so the two entities' claims are withdrawn and the two sites now take their better sources as primary. Re-sourced to the register: the provider counts in the Equinix, Digital Realty, Macquarie (now six sites, adding IC3e), DCI and Telstra notes, the framework's 'highest level of assurance' wording, and the Macquarie security record, which is derived from the register and now VERIFIED. The four capacity metrics it relays from Mandala and CBRE drop to low confidence. Marsden Park's application row now cites the portal and its assessment report. The Mandala report the article names (Data Centres as Enabling Infrastructure, November 2025, archived) does not state 1,350 MW or 3,100 MW, in megawatts or gigawatts, in its text (pages 46 and 47 of its 48 carry no text and were not read as images); it points to Mandala's October 2024 report, which this environment cannot fetch because the host's robots.txt refuses it, as does CDC's copy. CBRE answers 403. FROM THE ARCHIVED REGISTER (primary, SRC_HCF_REGISTER): its text names only 'the Department' and the page carries the Department of Home Affairs logo (corrected 2026-10-21: earlier notes overlooked the logo); it lists data centre facilities that match no site record here: Cloud Carrier DB1 (facility); Vocus TransACT House Dickson (enclave). RG-096 matched only existing records, so these are candidates for new site rows. LEADS ONLY, from search-engine summaries read on 2026-10-14 (below grade D, not relied on, and kept out of every fact row): the framework appears to have moved from the Digital Transformation Agency to Home Affairs on 1 May 2023 (the move and its date, not the current branding, are the lead); the 1,350 MW and 3,100 MW figures appear to come from Mandala's October 2024 report; and AustralianSuper appears to have announced a EUR 1.5bn minority investment in Vantage Data Centers' EMEA platform on 11 September 2023. UPDATED 2026-11-18 (research batch 8, second pass): The two Mandala figures now rest on Mandala: the October 2024 report says 'data centre deployable capacity in Australia is projected to more than double from 1,350 megawatts (MW) in 2024 to 3,100 MW by 2030', and that it 'was commissioned by AirTrunk, Amazon Web Services, CDC, Microsoft, and NEXTDC'. Read from the copy AirTrunk publishes; Mandala's own host had refused. The two metrics are re-sourced to it (REPORTED, medium: an industry-commissioned projection). STILL ON CertifiedStrategic.com alone: the two CBRE figures (CBRE answered 403) and the national count of certified facilities.

OPENED 2026-11-15 by the RG-084 merge. The seed row cited SRC_CERTSTRAT for 'A$264m', 'for AWS' and 'a north-zone start in September 2026'. The archived article (data/raw/operators/certifiedstrategic/) does not contain the word 'Stockland' - checked by this script and by curate_certstrat_review.py - so the citation never supported the claim. The consent itself records approval, not construction. Nothing here has been read that names an end user or a start date. Until one is, the surviving row keeps status 'approved' and no anchor tenant. One lead, no more: the NSW IDA release of 27 March 2026 lists 'Stockland Project A City of Ryde' (recorded separately as SITE_STOCKLAND_PROJA) and states '**NB: One IDA endorsed data centre not listed due to commercial sensitivities**'. Whether the withheld project is this one is unknown and is not assumed. UPDATED 2026-11-18 (research batch 7): CONSTRUCTION ANSWERED, END USER NOT. The Department's March 2026 report on the neighbouring SSD-63235720 describes 'an existing data centre adjoining to the west at 11-17 Khartoum Road (SSD-10467)' and lists, among adjoining sites, 'one operational data centre, one under-construction data centre, and one data centre currently under assessment'. So SSD-10467 was built and operating by March 2026. Its own 2021 report says only that 'The Applicant has been approached by a data centre operator (the lessee)' who would operate it: one of the nine unnamed operators (RG-055). PROPOSED for the author: SITE_MACQUARIE_PARK_DC status `approved` -> `operational`, REPORTED on the Department's description. Not made by this pack. DECIDED BY THE AUTHOR 2026-11-18 (research batch 7): Status set to operational. The end user stays unnamed, so the question stays open for it. UPDATED 2026-11-18 (research batch 8, second pass): One more free search (Stockland's releases and the trade press): no record names the end user. A directory's 'believed to be' a cloud provider is speculation, not a record. PROPOSED TO THE AUTHOR as not retrievable at zero spend; the question would re-open on an operator's or Stockland's own statement. Not closed by this pack.

Advanced again 2026-09-18. The complete NSW data centre SSD register (46 records) contains NO project titled AWS, Amazon, Google or Meta; Microsoft appears only through its proponent entity Microsoft Datacentre (Australia) Pty Ltd on Kemps Creek SSD-10101987 (approved, operating) and Honeman Close SSD-58601963 (in Assessment, description references 96 MW). Conclusion: hyperscaler footprints CANNOT be mapped from NSW planning titles. The sector's convention is codenames - Project Duke, Atlas, Echidna, Apollo, Pluto, Mars, KC1, Road 1 - and the NSW Government's own IDA release confirms it (Goodman's 'Project Atlas', Stockland's 'Project A'), with one endorsed project withheld entirely for commercial sensitivity. Remaining routes are ASIC resolution of the codename SPVs (RG-035), landlord tenancy disclosure, and Victorian and Queensland registers. AWS and Google remain entirely unresolved. UPDATED 2026-11-18 (research batch 8, second pass): PROPOSED TO THE AUTHOR: close the remainder (AWS's and Google's site-level footprints) as not retrievable at zero spend. The free routes are worked: planning registers name codename companies and consultancies, not hyperscalers (RG-035, RG-055); the landowner documents are restricted (GIPA-001, not lodged). Not closed by this pack.
